nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaches the canopy and the open ridges; cloud often cuts it back on the upper slopes.

nodes.name: Rain and cloud
nodes.desc: Moist air from the sea condenses on the mountain, keeping the montane forest wet and mossy.

nodes.name: Cool mountain air
nodes.desc: Temperature falls with height, so forest type changes from lowland to montane oak, rhododendron and conifer zones.

nodes.name: Mountain soil
nodes.desc: Thin, nutrient-poor mountain soils. Pitcher plants make up for scarce nitrogen by catching insects and animal droppings.

nodes.name: Montane oaks
nodes.desc: Stone oaks are among the trees of the montane forest zone, which Wikipedia describes as oak, then rhododendron and conifer forest as you climb.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Figs bear fruit that many forest birds and mammals eat. A fig species is among the commonly recorded plants near the park.

nodes.name: Rhododendrons
nodes.desc: Flowering shrubs of the higher forest zones, which provide nectar and flowers for birds.

nodes.name: Giant pitcher plant
nodes.desc: A carnivorous plant and the most notable pitcher plant of the park. Tree shrews and summit rats lick nectar from its lid and defecate into the pitcher.

nodes.name: Rafflesia
nodes.desc: A parasitic flowering plant that lives inside a host vine and shows itself only as a huge flower; endemic to Sabah.

nodes.name: Mountain treeshrew
nodes.desc: Eats mostly arthropods plus wild fruit, and licks nectar from pitcher plants including N. rajah, leaving droppings in them. Endemic to Borneo.

nodes.name: Summit rat
nodes.desc: A night-active rat that licks nectar from giant pitcher lids and defecates into them; one of the most recorded mammals near the park.

nodes.name: Jentink's squirrel
nodes.desc: A small squirrel of montane Borneo forest, recorded often near the park.

nodes.name: Golden-naped barbet
nodes.desc: A montane Bornean bird recorded thousands of times near the park; barbets in general take fruit such as figs.

nodes.name: Temminck's sunbird
nodes.desc: A small nectar-feeding bird of Bornean mountain forest, among the most recorded birds near the park.

nodes.name: Three-horned rhinoceros beetle
nodes.desc: A large beetle of the montane forest. Rhinoceros beetle larvae of this kind develop in rotting wood; adults are prey for forest birds and frogs.

nodes.name: Montane large-eyed litter frog
nodes.desc: A frog of the forest floor that eats small invertebrates.

nodes.name: Bornean whistling thrush
nodes.desc: A bird of mountain streams and forest floor that feeds on insects and other small animals.

nodes.name: Bornean treepie
nodes.desc: The most recorded bird near the park; an omnivorous crow relative that takes fruit and small animals.

nodes.name: Chestnut-crested yuhina
nodes.desc: A busy flocking bird that takes insects and fruit; one of the most recorded birds near the park.

nodes.name: Sabah bamboo pitviper
nodes.desc: A Bornean pitviper of mountain forest, usually seen on branches of shrubs; it takes small vertebrates such as frogs and rodents.

nodes.name: Fungi, leeches & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and dead animals in the damp forest floor and return nutrients to the soil.
